36 notes change pitch, waveform or pulse width while sounding (wavetable, vibrato, arpeggio, glide, pulse sweep); the program holds one value of each per note.
12 changes of the filter or volume registers between note starts are not written; the values are updated at note starts only.

Records are timed with TI (60 Hz, 16.7 ms steps) and the interpreter writes one register about every 10 ms: predicted note start error 7 ms mean, 61 ms maximum; the phase of TI adds up to 17 ms, and gate-offs are less exact than note starts. 62 gate-offs shortly before the next note of a voice are written together with that note.
4 events are too dense for BASIC V2 and are delayed by more than 25 ms, at most 61 ms (predicted). --voices 2 or 1 writes fewer registers.

Drum voices (v3) are not exported: SID-Wizard drums are instruments, which this export does not build from SIDWave kits.
Rows are one player call long (note starts and ends fall on odd calls): the module is correct but large and uses the fastest tempo.
Note velocities (3 distinct values) are not exported; the module plays at full volume.
